CONTAINERS  a per-sandbox engine behind a filtering proxy at /run/snug/podman.sock
         Containers run in THIS sandbox's own network namespace: with no
         '@net', a container has no egress either; with '@net', full egress
         via the sandbox's pasta, exactly as the NETWORK block above states.
         A container has the sandbox's own network with NO port mapping:
         'podman run -p N:80' is not supported — the engine holds no
         CAP_NET_ADMIN, so it cannot reconfigure this namespace to publish one.
         A container gets its own pid namespace and may not join another:
         'podman run --pid=host' is refused. Inside the sandbox 'host' would
         mean the ENGINE, and /proc/<pid>/root in a shared pid namespace
         reaches that process's entire filesystem view.
         A container may mount only a path the sandbox can already see,
         enforced by the proxy's bind filter, which reads this same resolved
         policy (the mount view itself is still a private copy of the host
         tree, not a derived one — see the TOPOLOGY block).
IMAGES   provenance is snug's, not this host's (issue #137)
         search      docker.io and nothing else — no mirror, no rewrite, no
                     insecure registry. A generated registries.conf, pointed
                     at by CONTAINERS_REGISTRIES_CONF
         signatures  NOT verified: snug generates the engine's policy.json
                     (accept anything), so the host's own cannot decide it.
                     A host policy stricter than that is named on stderr
                     before the run starts
         logins      NONE. REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE points at an empty file, so the
                     host's ~/.docker/config.json and auth.json are not read,
                     and no private image can be pulled (issue #142)
         home        the engine gets a HOME of its own for the same reason —
                     everything podman reads out of one is snug's or absent
